keyword: git remote 주소 변경 (git remote set-url)

sources.title: git-remote Documentation
sources.body: SYNOPSIS (verbatim): git remote [-v | --verbose] / git remote add [-t <branch>] [-m <master>] [-f] [--[no-]tags] [--mirror=(fetch|push)] <name> <URL> / git remote rename [--[no-]progress] <old> <new> / git remote remove <name> / git remote get-url [--push] [--all] <name> / git remote set-url [--push] <name> <newurl> [<oldurl>] / git remote set-url --add [--push] <name> <newurl> / git remote set-url --delete [--push] <name> <URL>. -v: 'Be a little more verbose and show remote url after name. ... NOTE: This must be placed between remote and subcommand.' set-url: 'Change URLs for the remote. Sets first URL for remote <name> that matches regex <oldurl> (first URL if no <oldurl> is given) to <newurl>. If <oldurl> doesn't match any URL, an error occurs and nothing is changed. With --push, push URLs are manipulated instead of fetch URLs. With --add, instead of changing existing URLs, new URL is added. With --delete, instead of changing existing URLs, all URLs matching regex <URL> are deleted for remote <name>. Trying to delete all non-push URLs is an error. Note that the push URL and the fetch URL, even though they can be set differently, must still refer to the same place. What you pushed to the push URL should be what you would see if you immediately fetched from the fetch URL. If you are trying to fetch from one place (e.g. your upstream) and push to another (e.g. your publishing repository), use two separate remotes.' rename: 'Rename the remote named <old> to <new>. All remote-tracking branches and configuration settings for the remote are updated.' remove/rm: 'Remove the remote named <name>. All remote-tracking branches and configuration settings for the remote are removed.' get-url: 'Retrieves the URLs for a remote. Configurations for insteadOf and pushInsteadOf are expanded here. By default, only the first URL is listed. With --push, push URLs are queried rather than fetch URLs. With --all, all URLs for the remote will be listed.' add: 'Add a remote named <name> for the repository at <URL>. The command git fetch <name> can then be used to create and update remote-tracking branches <name>/<branch>.' The page has no EXAMPLES entry for set-url.
facts: set-url syntax: git remote set-url [--push] <name> <newurl> [<oldurl>]; without <oldurl> the first URL is changed; if <oldurl> matches nothing, error and nothing changed
--push manipulates push URLs instead of fetch URLs; --add adds a URL; --delete removes all URLs matching regex
git remote -v: -v must be placed between 'remote' and the subcommand
rename updates all remote-tracking branches and config for the remote; remove deletes remote-tracking branches and config settings
Docs warn push URL and fetch URL must still refer to the same place; for fetch from upstream and push to another repo use two separate remotes
get-url expands insteadOf / pushInsteadOf; --push, --all options

sources.title: Managing remote repositories - GitHub Docs
sources.body: Viewing: `git remote -v` prints '> origin  https://github.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY.git (fetch)' and '(push)'. Adding: 'To add a new remote, use the git remote add command on the terminal, in the directory your repository is stored at.' Example: git remote add origin https://github.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY.git. Changing URL: 'The git remote set-url command changes an existing remote repository URL.' Example: git remote set-url origin https://github.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY.git. HTTPS to SSH: 'Change your remote's URL from HTTPS to SSH with the git remote set-url command.' Example: git remote set-url origin git@github.com:OWNER/REPOSITORY.git. Renaming: 'Use the git remote rename command to rename an existing remote.' Example: git remote rename origin destination. Removing: 'Use the git remote rm command to remove a remote URL from your repository.' 'Removing the remote URL from your repository only unlinks the local and remote repositories.' Example: git remote rm destination.
facts: git remote -v output shows origin <URL> (fetch) and (push) lines
HTTPS->SSH: git remote set-url origin git@github.com:OWNER/REPOSITORY.git
git remote rename origin destination
git remote rm destination: 'only unlinks the local and remote repositories' (remote repo is not deleted)

sources.title: Renaming a repository - GitHub Docs
sources.body: Redirects: 'all existing information, with the exception of project site URLs, is automatically redirected to the new name' (issues, wikis, stars, followers). Web traffic is redirected; git operations to the old location 'will continue to function as if made on the new location.' Local clones keep the old URL; GitHub recommends updating them to reduce confusion: git remote set-url origin NEW_URL. Limitations: GitHub Pages project site URLs are not redirected (use custom domain). Workflows that call an action from a renamed repository fail with 'repository not found' because GitHub does not redirect these calls. Do not create a new repository with the old name; that breaks the redirects to the renamed repository. Only organization owners or repository admins can rename a repository.
facts: After rename, git operations to old URL still work via redirect, but docs recommend git remote set-url origin NEW_URL
Pages project site URLs are excluded from redirect
Actions referencing renamed repo fail with 'repository not found' (no redirect)
Creating a new repo with the old name breaks the redirects
Only org owners or repo admins can rename

sources.title: Transferring a repository - GitHub Docs
sources.body: 'All links to the previous repository location are automatically redirected to the new location.' 'When you use git clone, git fetch, or git push on a transferred repository, these commands will redirect to the new repository location or URL.' 'To avoid confusion, we strongly recommend updating any existing local clones to point to the new repository URL.' Do so with git remote set-url origin NEW_URL. Web: links to the Git repository on the Web and through Git activity are redirected; 'we don't redirect GitHub Pages associated with the repository.' Redirect breaks: creating a new repository or fork at the old location means 'the redirects to the transferred repository will be permanently deleted.' If the repository contained a GitHub Marketplace action or had over 100 clones or GitHub Actions uses in the prior week, the old owner/name combination is permanently retired; creating a repository with it fails with 'has been retired and cannot be reused.'
facts: clone/fetch/push to transferred repo's old URL redirect to the new location
Docs 'strongly recommend' updating local clones: git remote set-url origin NEW_URL
New repo/fork at the old location permanently deletes the redirects
Marketplace action or >100 clones or Actions uses in prior week: old owner/name permanently retired ('has been retired and cannot be reused')
GitHub Pages not redirected

sources.title: Pro Git 2.5 Git Basics - Working with Remotes
sources.body: git remote -v: 'shows you the URLs that Git has stored for the shortname to be used when reading and writing to that remote' (origin https://github.com/schacon/ticgit (fetch)/(push)). Add: 'run git remote add <shortname> <url>' e.g. git remote add pb https://github.com/paulboone/ticgit; 'Now you can use the string pb on the command line instead of the whole URL.' Rename: git remote rename pb paul; 'this changes all your remote-tracking branch names, too. What used to be referenced at pb/master is now at paul/master.' Remove: 'If you want to remove a remote for some reason - you have moved the server or are no longer using a particular mirror ... you can either use git remote remove or git remote rm'; 'Once you delete the reference to a remote this way, all remote-tracking branches and configuration settings associated with that remote are also deleted.'
facts: git remote add <shortname> <url>
git remote rename pb paul changes remote-tracking branch names: pb/master -> paul/master
git remote remove / rm deletes remote-tracking branches and configuration settings of that remote
git clone implicitly adds the origin remote
